"Bidiots" - Great bloody game as well, not sure it would be able to stand on it's own, but it will give you a couple hours of good fun - I am not done with this yet myself, despite me often starting this game to play Fibbage 2 more so than anything else.

Pack 2; honestly I think this pack got a rough deal within my group. As with most of the earlier packs, Pack 2 had its priced raised with the release of Pack 9/10, so I'll be approaching this as "is this worth £21 in 2025". And though I'll admit it got unfairly derided by my friends, it's... still not great.

Quiplash XL: Succeeded by Quiplash 2 and 3. I don't actually like 3 that much for the final round, and honestly of all the "series" titles Jackbox has it holds up the best by far; but for twenty five dollars... eh...

Bidiots: An interesting premise that is doing a lot of different things; the combination of the tips and the screws mechanics mean you have to be really dialled in to everything that's going on, and for the "party game" vibe it just hasn't gelled for everyone I've played with. Generally though I'd love to see an updated version of this game - probably the strongest in the pack.

Fibbage 2: Successor to Fibbage XL, and succeded by Fibbage 3 and 4, the game is unfortunately outmatched in quality and design by later iterations.

Earwax: Actually a run fun design for gameplay, but the scoring system can make the game either incredibly short or incredibly long. The number of sound effects is also somewhat limited, so even in one game you can end up recycling answers. Another one I wish had a modern update, but is still fairly solid for a couple of games. 

Bomb Corp: "Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes" but as a party game - if your group loves it then this can make or break the pack alongside Earwax and Bidiots in my opinion, but if it's too long for you then I think the pack overall isn't worth it. 

Overall Pack 2 has a few hit-or-miss gems, but for twenty plus dollars the flaws are just a little too prominent to be worth it. Pack 2 is our least-played by a wide margin, despite being released ten years ago, and for good reason. Not worth its new price.
